newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell 10 pct of MIB.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell 10 pct of MIB.

text.p: The state-owned Banque Misr said on Sunday it was offering to the private sector 10 percent of Misr International Bank (MIB) at 310 pounds each.
Banque Misr owns 55.65 percent of MIB's 3.75 million shares.
The offer for 375,000 shares will be open for individuals, mutual funds and investment firms on Monday only.
Banque Misr said shareholders would be eligible for an unspecified dividend and a 1/4 bonus share for the 1996 financial year, which ends on December 31.
The state's Misr Insurance owns four percent and Egyptian individuals own 11.35 percent.

Foreign investors include Banca di Roma International (10 percent), British Arab Commercial Bank (8.5 percent) Commerzbank and Central Hispano Americano Banco (jointly 7.875 percent) and Sakura Bank Limited (2.625 percent).

MIB, which has a capital of $37.5 million, earlier this month said that its net profits rose 60 percent in the first half of calendar year 1996 to 64 million pounds from 40 million pounds for the same period of 1995.
The bank's total assets rose to 9,034 million pounds on June 30, 1996, from 7,823 million one year earlier.
